table_title: List the top 20 largest lakes in the world by surface area per the Wikipedia 'List of lakes by area' master article (Table[2] area-descending ranking), with each lake's continent, water type (Fresh or Saline), surface area in square kilometres, and maximum depth in metres.
db_analog: SELECT lake, continent, type, area_km2, max_depth_m FROM lakes ORDER BY area_km2 DESC LIMIT 20
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of lakes by area' master article, accessed 2026-05-14. Universe is the top-20 lakes by surface area per the master article's Table[2] area-descending ranking (Table[2] per pandas.read_html — 47-row master ordered by Area km² descending, with columns Thumbnail / Rank / Name / Countries with shoreline / Type / Area / Length / Max. depth / Volume / Notes). The top-20 cutoff is a hard rank-based filter on the source's own ordering — no curator-judgment on which lakes qualify; the staged 20 rows are precisely the source's first 20 by Rank. Per-row cells: Lake name verbatim from the master Name column ('Caspian Sea', 'Superior', 'Victoria', 'Malawi (Nyasa)', 'Great Bear Lake', 'Great Slave Lake', etc.); Continent is curator-derived from the master's 'Countries with shoreline' column using a closed 6-value vocabulary (Africa / Antarctica / Asia / Europe / North America / South America) with the rule: lakes with all shoreline-countries on a single continent take that continent; the Caspian Sea has shoreline in 5 transcontinental/Asian countries (Iran, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Azerbaijan, Russia) and is staged as 'Asia' per the dominant geographic position (4 of 5 shoreline countries are wholly or primarily Asian; Russia's Caspian shoreline is in its southern transcontinental region); Lake Vostok is staged as 'Antarctica' per its subglacial location under the Antarctic ice sheet; Type is curator-normalized from the master's Type column to a closed 2-value vocabulary (Fresh / Saline) by stripping salinity-percentage suffixes — within the staged top-20 only 2 rows are Saline ('Saline 1.2%' → 'Saline' for Caspian Sea rank-1; 'Saline 0.3% (variable)' → 'Saline' for Balkhash rank-15) and the other 18 are 'Fresh' verbatim; Area (km²) is the integer square-kilometre value extracted from the master Area column's compound '###,### km2 ###,### sq mi' formulation (comma-stripped); Max. depth (m) is the integer metre value extracted from the master Max. depth column's compound '###,### m ###,### ft' formulation (comma-stripped). The 20-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon: bathymetric and shoreline measurements may refine individual area/depth values, but the lake identifications and ordering of the top-20 by area are well-established (the Caspian Sea / Superior / Victoria / Huron / Michigan / Tanganyika / Baikal top-7 has been stable for decades; rank-20 Athabasca is unlikely to be displaced by any sub-rank-20 lake).
_extraction_notes: Original instance chipping `top_k` from gap 2 to **gap 1** (4 of 5 staged; existing 3: largest_islands_by_area_top20_britannica, top_10_most_populous_cities_per_continent, notable_bridges_by_main_span). User selected lakes-by-area after a deep-dive on the multi_hop capitals-rivers alternative which would have required curator-bounded universe + multi-source extraction; lakes-by-area is single-source single-master-table with all cells exact-match-evaluable. NEW `physical-features/lakes` fine-class extending the physical-features entity bucket from 6 fine-classes (mountains, rivers, deserts, islands, oceanic-trenches, +1 historical) to 7 with NEW lakes. NEW Geography/Lakes subdomain extending the Geography family from 11 to 12 instances. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 1 — the master 'List of lakes by area' Wikipedia article supplies all 5 cells per row via its Table[2] area-descending wikitable. Pipeline: (1) fetch the cited Wikipedia article HTML, (2) parse tables[2] (47-row master area-descending wikitable with columns Name / Countries / Type / Area / Length / Max. depth / Volume / Notes), (3) take the top-20 rows by Rank (= top-20 by area; no filter beyond rank cutoff), (4) for each row: take Lake name verbatim from the Name column; derive Continent from the Countries-with-shoreline cell using the dominant-continent rule; normalize Type to Fresh/Saline by stripping salinity-percentage suffixes; extract Area (km²) as integer from the master Area column's '###,### km2 ###,### sq mi' format (comma-stripped); extract Max. depth (m) as integer from the master Max. depth column's '###,### m ###,### ft' format (comma-stripped). Result: 20 rows × 5 columns, PK on Lake, 0 duplicates. Continent distribution: North America 10 (Superior, Huron, Michigan, Great Bear Lake, Great Slave Lake, Erie, Winnipeg, Ontario, Nicaragua, Athabasca), Africa 3 (Victoria, Tanganyika, Malawi/Nyasa), Asia 3 (Caspian Sea, Baikal, Balkhash), Europe 2 (Ladoga, Onega), Antarctica 1 (Vostok), South America 1 (Titicaca) — sum 20. Type distribution: Fresh 18, Saline 2 (Caspian Sea, Balkhash). Area range: 389,000 km² (Caspian Sea, rank 1) to 7,850 km² (Athabasca, rank 20). Max depth range: 26 m (Balkhash, Nicaragua tied) to 1,642 m (Baikal — deepest lake in the world). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical great lakes (Caspian Sea, Superior, Victoria, Tanganyika, Baikal, Titicaca, Erie, Ontario); mid-difficulty cells include the well-known but less-headline-grabbing lakes (Huron, Michigan, Great Bear, Great Slave, Malawi, Ladoga, Winnipeg); harder calibration cells include the less-headline-grabbing lakes (Balkhash, Vostok subglacial, Onega, Nicaragua, Athabasca). The Caspian Sea is staged as a lake per the source's classification despite being geologically a 'small ocean' (source's own Notes column addresses this and rules in favor of lake classification per surface-area-ranking convention). Vostok subglacial lake is staged with Continent = Antarctica per its location. Sort order: CSV is sorted by Area (km²) descending (= source's Rank ascending) matching the master article's natural area-ranking order. The deepest cell (Baikal, 1,642 m) demonstrates that area-rank and depth-rank are decorrelated (Baikal is rank-7 by area but #1 by depth); area is the staged ranking attribute.
